about.title: Covina Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Covina's stretch of San Gabriel Valley roadways carries a steady mix of local traffic and commuters cutting through on Citrus Avenue and San Bernardino Road. Public records show 117 injury collisions and 165 injured people in the most recent final crash year, with Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing the heaviest concentration of reported crashes. Behind each of those numbers is a person dealing with medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster who may call before the dust even settles. We handle personal injury claims for injured Covina residents, reviewing the details of your crash and the local circumstances. Los Angeles County traffic can move fast at intersections along these corridors, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, and witness memory fades quickly. Our team understands local roads and California claims, helping you avoid early mistakes.
about.commonInjuriesTitle: Injuries We Commonly See After Covina Car Accidents
about.ctaText: Contact us for a free case review—no obligation.

items.title: Your Time Window Is Limited
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Connecting with us early helps make sure that deadline doesn't slip by unnoticed.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Shut the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you're found partly responsible for the crash—your recovery is simply adjusted to reflect your share. We can help make sure your percentage of fault isn't overstated by the other side.

items.title: No Recorded Statement, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often want a recorded statement early, which can be used against you later—we can speak for you instead. We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you actually recover money.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash near Grand Avenue and Badillo Street—what should I do first?
items.answer: Seek medical care first, even if injuries seem minor, since some symptoms surface days later. Try to document the scene with photos if you're able, and avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer. From there, contacting us can help preserve evidence before it disappears.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Covina car accident?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. That window shortens significantly, sometimes to six months, if a government entity or vehicle was involved. Because these deadlines are strict, it's wise to get guidance sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if the insurance company says I was partly at fault?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover damages even if you share some blame for the crash. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't eliminated. We can push back if the insurer tries to inflate your share unfairly.
